t: 유월절(Passover / Pesach) — 어린양, 피, 바다, 그리고 부활하신 메시아
타즈리아-메쪼라 Tazria-Mezora '- — 생명의 잉태와 탄생, 부정함, 나병
아하레이 모트-케도쉼 Acharei Mot-Kedoshim — “죽음 후에 & 거룩한 자들”
히브리 달력 6월 엘룰 — 왕께로 돌아가고, 숨겨진 기초를 준비하며, 수용력을 넓혀 다음 계절을 위해 건축하는 달
키 테쩨 Ki Tetze — 네가 나갈 때 When You Go
키 타보 Ki Tavo — 네가 돌아올 때 When You Come
라쉬 하샤나 Rosh HaShanah — 나팔절 Festival of Trumpets
하아지누 Ha’azinu — 귀를 기울이라 Give Ear
욤키푸르 Yom Kippur — 대속죄일 Day of Atonement & 쑤콭 Sukkot — 초막절
Hi, I'm Peter. It's so nice to meet you.
s: 안녕하세요, 저는 피터예요. 만나서 정말 반가워요.

t: What's your name again? Sorry, I didn't catch it.
s: 이름이 다시 뭐였죠? 죄송해요, 제가 못 들었어요.

t: How long have you lived here?
Actually, this is my first time here.
I don't speak much English, but I'll do my best.
s: 저는 영어를 잘 못하지만 최선을 다해볼게요.

t: It's really nice to meet you.
I'd really like to get to know you better.
It was great talking with you.
Nice to finally meet you in person.
I've heard a lot about you.
How do you two know each other?

s: 죄송한데, 저희 전에 만난 적 있나요?

t: I'm still learning English, so please bear with me.
s: 제가 아직 영어를 배우는 중이라, 조금만 이해해 주세요.

t: I've been here for about three months.
s: 여기 온 지 세 달쯤 됐어요.

t: I'm just visiting for a little while.
I live just down the street.
s: 저는 바로 이 길 아래쪽에 살아요.

t: I came here with my church.
It's a small world, isn't it?
Do you mind if I join you?
I don't think we've met. I'm Peter.
s: 우리 아직 인사 안 한 것 같네요. 저는 피터예요.

t: Let me introduce you to my friend.
I'm so glad we got to meet.
The weather's really nice today, isn't it?
So, what do you do for work?
What do you like to do for fun?
I'm still trying to figure out the culture here.
s: 저는 아직 이곳 문화를 이해하려고 노력 중이에요.

t: I had such a great time today.
Did you do anything fun this weekend?
What have you been up to lately?
What part of town do you live in?
I was just thinking the same thing.
s: 저도 딱 같은 생각 하고 있었어요.

t: You've got to be kidding me.
I'm really sorry to hear that.
That must have been so hard.
I'm not so sure about that.
Sorry, are you saying I should wait here?
s: 죄송한데, 제가 여기서 기다려야 한다는 말씀이신가요?

t: Just to be clear, we're meeting at six?
s: 확실히 하자면, 우리 여섯 시에 만나는 거죠?

t: Could you go over that one more time?
How do you say this in English?

s: 죄송해요, 제가 아직 영어를 배우는 중이에요.

t: Could you speak a little slower, please?
Is that how you say it?
Could you write it down for me?
I think I understand, but let me make sure.
So, if I understood correctly, we leave at eight?
s: 그러니까 제가 제대로 이해했다면, 여덟 시에 출발하는 거죠?

t: Sorry, I zoned out for a second.
Could you repeat the last part?
I'm sorry, I don't know that word.
Sorry, I mixed up my words.
Thanks for being patient with me.
Excuse me, could you help me for a second?
I'm trying to find this address.
Sorry, could you say that one more time?
Sorry, I'm not quite following you.
s: 죄송한데, 제가 잘 이해가 안 돼서요.

t: Would you mind speaking a little slower?
Excuse me, is there a restroom nearby?
Would you mind writing that down for me?
Thank you so much, I really appreciate it.
Excuse me, do you know where the station is?
Could you point me in the right direction?
Am I going the right way?
s: 제가 맞는 방향으로 가고 있는 건가요?

t: How do I get to the bus station?
Is there a bus that goes there?
How long does it take to get there?
Could you show me on the map?
Do you know if there's a pharmacy around here?
Could you call a taxi for me?
Do you mind if I ask you something?
Sorry to bother you, but could you help me?
Would you be able to help me with this?
Can you walk me through it?
I could really use your help.
Thanks, you've been a huge help.
I don't know what I would have done without you.
Please, come on in and have a seat.
Can I get you something to drink?
Thanks so much for having me.
Your family has been so kind to me.
s: 당신 가족이 저에게 정말 친절하게 대해주셨어요.

t: I'd love to come back and visit again sometime.
Just let me know if you need anything at all.
I really appreciate everything you've done for me.
s: 저를 위해 해주신 모든 것에 정말 감사해요.

t: Can I give you a hand with that?
This is delicious. Did you make it yourself?
Thank you for the wonderful meal.
Text me when you get home.
I'd love to have you over sometime.
s: 언제 한번 저희 집에 초대하고 싶어요.

t: Would you like to grab coffee sometime?
Thank you for thinking of me.
Oh, you didn't have to do that.
I really enjoy spending time with you.
You mean a lot to me.
I believe God loves you so much.
s: 저는 하나님이 당신을 정말 많이 사랑하신다고 믿어요.

t: Would it be okay if I shared something with you?
I came here because of my faith.
s: 저는 제 믿음 때문에 여기 왔어요.

t: Would you like to hear my story sometime?
I'm really grateful for God's grace in my life.
s: 제 삶 속 하나님의 은혜에 정말 감사해요.

t: Can I ask what you believe about God?
s: 하나님에 대해 어떻게 믿으시는지 물어봐도 될까요?

t: I'd love for you to come check out our gathering sometime.
s: 언젠가 저희 모임에 한번 와보시면 좋겠어요.

t: I truly believe God has a plan for your life.
s: 저는 하나님이 당신의 삶에 계획이 있다고 진심으로 믿어요.

t: How can I pray for you?

s: 제가 당신을 위해 계속 기도해 왔어요.
저는 이 일을 하나님께 맡기고 있어요.

t: God has been so good to me.
Do you go to church anywhere?
I'd love to invite you to church this Sunday.
Church starts at ten. Would you like to come with me?
s: 예배는 열 시에 시작해요. 저랑 같이 가실래요?

t: I believe God brought me here for a reason.
s: 저는 하나님이 이유가 있어 저를 여기 보내셨다고 믿어요.

t: I don't have all the answers, but I know God is with me.
s: 제가 모든 답을 아는 건 아니지만, 하나님이 저와 함께하신다는 건 알아요.

t: That's a really good question. Let me think about it.
s: 정말 좋은 질문이에요. 좀 생각해 볼게요.

t: Thank you for being so open with me.
I'm not here to argue. I just want you to know you're loved.
s: 저는 논쟁하러 온 게 아니에요. 그저 당신이 사랑받고 있다는 걸 알려드리고 싶어요.

t: God saw me at my lowest and didn't walk away.
s: 하나님은 제가 가장 밑바닥에 있을 때 저를 보시고도 떠나지 않으셨어요.

t: I used to feel completely empty inside.
s: 저는 예전엔 속이 완전히 텅 빈 것 같았어요.

t: I found real peace for the first time.
Would it be okay if we prayed about it together right now?
I'll be praying for you and your family.
I think I need to see a doctor.
s: 저 병원에 가봐야 할 것 같아요.

t: Could someone please call for help?
I think I lost my passport.
Is it safe to walk around here at night?
I need to find somewhere to stay tonight.
s: 오늘 밤 머물 곳을 찾아야 해요.

t: Could I borrow your phone? It's kind of an emergency.
s: 전화 좀 빌려도 될까요? 좀 급한 일이라서요.

t: Thank you so much for keeping me safe.
I have to take medicine every day.
I've had a headache since this morning.
I think I sprained my ankle.
Do I need a prescription for this?
Could I charge my phone somewhere?
Where do I pick up my luggage?
I'd like to report a stolen wallet.
Could you help me find the Korean embassy?
Can I get a coffee, please?
Do you have this in a different size?
Can I get this to go?
Could we get the check, please?
Excuse me, I think there's a mistake on the bill.
s: 실례합니다, 계산서에 착오가 있는 것 같아요.
죄송한데, 저 줄 서 있는 거예요.

t: Go ahead, I'm not in a hurry.
Do you know what time you close?
Could you make it a little less spicy?
s: 조금만 덜 맵게 해주실 수 있을까요?

t: It was really good, thank you.
Could I get some more napkins?
I'm a little under the weather.

s: 그 덕분에 오늘 하루가 정말 좋았어요.

t: I'm not really in the mood today.
I didn't mean it that way.
That means a lot to me.
s: 그 말이 저에겐 정말 큰 의미예요.

t: I'm happy right where I am.
I'll be there in ten minutes.
I'll pick you up at six.
Can I get back to you on that?
We'll cross that bridge when we get there.
I can't make it, but thanks for asking.
s: 저는 못 갈 것 같아요, 그래도 물어봐 주셔서 감사해요.

t: Could you give me a hand with this?
What do you want me to do?
Just let me know if you need anything.
Do you want me to help?
Just let me know when you're ready.

s: 제가 한 번 더 확인해 볼게요.

t: Can you hold this for a second?
Could you move a little to the left?
Let's try it one more time.
Can I ask you something real quick?
I'm not sure. What would you do?
We couldn't have done it without you.
Winning here is a conscious decision.
Make up your mind whether you want to pass or choose to fail.
s: 통과할지, 아니면 실패를 선택할지 마음을 정하세요.

t: Take all this shaking and all this cold, and turn it into aggression.
s: 이 떨림과 이 추위를 전부 받아들이고, 그것을 공격성으로 바꾸세요.

t: You just proved to your body, through your mind, that you can push yourself further than y
s: 당신은 방금 마음을 통해 몸에게 증명했습니다. 생각했던 것보다 더 멀리 자신을 밀어붙일 수 있다는 것을요.

t: Whatever you have to do, just find an excuse to win.
s: 무엇을 해야 하든, 그냥 이길 핑계를 찾으세요.

t: Keep going. It pays to be a winner.
s: 계속하세요. 승자가 되는 건 그만한 가치가 있습니다.

t: Are you absolutely sure? I'm positive.
I have buddies I can depend on, and I want them to be able to depend on me too.
s: 저에게는 의지할 수 있는 동료들이 있고, 저도 그들이 저에게 의지할 수 있으면 좋겠어요.

t: You guys are our band of brothers.
s: 여러분은 우리의 밴드 오브 브라더스, 즉 전우입니다.

t: The only easy day was yesterday.
Slow is smooth, and smooth is fast.
Don't quit on a bad day.
One more step. That's all you need right now.
s: 한 걸음만 더. 지금 필요한 건 그것뿐이에요.

t: Discipline is doing what needs to be done, even when you don't want to.
s: 규율이란 하기 싫을 때도 해야 할 일을 하는 것입니다.

t: Pain is temporary. Quitting lasts forever.

s: 아무도 신경 쓰지 않는다. 더 열심히 해라.

t: You're better than you think you are, and you can do more than you think you can.
s: 당신은 스스로 생각하는 것보다 더 강하고, 할 수 있다고 믿는 것보다 더 많은 것을 해낼 수 있습니다.

t: 회식 강요 문화 vs 개인 시간
표현의 자유 vs 혐오 발언 규제

s: Entropy and the arrow of time
